'''Robert Anthony Vaden''' (born March 3, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Previously he played for the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. Vaden played [[college basketball]] with the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] and the [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB Blazers]] for two years each. After four years in college, he was drafted by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] with the 54th pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. After the draft, his draft rights were immediately traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. However, the Thunder did not sign him to a contract. As a result, he went on to play in [[Legadue Basket|Italy]], Slovakia, and in the [[NBA Development League]] with the [[Tulsa 66ers]], the D-League team affiliated with the Thunder.

==High school career==
Robert Vaden attended [[Cathedral High School (Indianapolis)|Cathedral High School]] and [[Pike High School]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]] and [[Bridgton Academy]] in [[Bridgton, Maine]]. As a senior at Bridgton Academy, Vaden averaged 26 points and 8 rebounds per game, leading the team to a 27–7 record. He played his freshman and sophomore years at Cathedral, before leaving due to a dispute between his parental guardian and the school. He went on to play his junior year at Pike, where he led the Red Devils to an undefeated record (29–0) and the Indiana Class 4A title. He averaged 13.5 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game.

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Vaden was listed as the No. 8 small forward and the No. 38 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Robert-Vaden-10587;_ylt=AoXT5HZc_2_c7EPJ_DugAyfXO5B4 Robert Vaden Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Vaden began his career at [[Indiana University]], where he started every game in his first two years. In his freshman season, he led the Hoosiers in minutes played (980), free throw percentage (.803), and steals per game (1.55 – fifth in the Big Ten). He was the team's third-leading scorer (10.5) and rebounder (4.3).

In his sophomore campaign, Vaden emerged as one of the top players in the Big Ten. He finished second on the team in scoring (13.5) and rebounding (5.5), while leading the squad in assists (109) and steals (38). The season featured many memorable moments for Vaden, as he had a streak of 12 consecutive three-pointers over a three-game stretch – only three short of the [[NCAA]] record. He also set the IU record for three-point percentage in a game, hitting 6–6 in a 12/31/05 game against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]]. Another high point came in the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006 NCAA Tournament]], where Vaden hit the game-winning three-pointer to lift the Hoosiers over [[San Diego State Aztecs|San Diego State]] in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/264000008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407152223/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/264000008|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2022|title=San Diego State 83–87 Indiana (Mar 16, 2006) Game Recap|website=ESPN}}</ref>

At the end of the 2005–06 season, Indiana coach [[Mike Davis (basketball coach)|Mike Davis]] was fired after failing to live up to the high Hoosier expectations, and later accepted the head coaching post at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]]. Vaden had grown close to his coach when Davis had supported him through his father's death after his freshman year at Indiana and chose to transfer to UAB to continue playing for him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/ncb/id/3254920|title=Showcase: UAB star Vaden makes huge leap for loyalty to coach|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

After sitting out the 2006–07 season due to NCAA transfer policy, Robert Vaden had a breakout junior year, logging one of the best seasons ever for a UAB player. He averaged 21.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game on the way to first team all-conference honors and being named the [[Conference USA]] Newcomer of the year. He set school records for points in a season (695), three-pointers made (142) and three-pointers attempted (355). His 142 three-pointers made were also a conference record and placed him second in the nation in this category. He also holds the UAB career record for scoring average (minimum 25 games) entering his senior year. On February 27, 2008, Vaden hit for 41 points, his career high, in a game against [[UTEP Miners|UTEP]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/280582638|title=UAB 88–81 UTEP (Feb 27, 2008) Box Score|website=ESPN}}</ref>

Vaden finished his college career with 2,010 points and hit 379 three-pointers in his career – good for #10 in NCAA history. He owns the UAB single-season records for points, three-pointers made, and attempted and is the school single-game record holder in points (41 – tied with [[Andy Kennedy (basketball coach)|Andy Kennedy]]), three-point field goals (9), and free throw percentage (11–11, tied with two others).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/schools/albr/graphics/mediaguides/08-m-baskbl/123-152_rec-hist.pdf |title=UAB men's basketball media guide – Record Book<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2008-12-28 |archive-date=2011-05-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110523103301/http://grfx.cstv.com/schools/albr/graphics/mediaguides/08-m-baskbl/123-152_rec-hist.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Vaden was [[Eligibility for the NBA Draft|automatically eligible]] for the [[2009 NBA draft]] after finishing his four-year college eligibility. He was projected to be either a second-round pick or [[Undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]] free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.al.com/uabbasketball/birminghamnews/index.ssf?/base/sports/124583143032960.xml&coll=2|title=UAB's Robert Vaden might not be drafted but could have NBA future|date=June 24, 2009|first=Ethan|last=Ramsey|work=The Birmingham News|publisher=Alabama Live LLC|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2009-06-24-242513360_x.htm|title=Gee, Vaden hoping to land with NBA teams|date=June 24, 2009|work=USA Today|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> He was eventually drafted by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] with the 54th pick in the draft and his rights were immediately traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/draft_release_090625.html|title=Thunder Acquires James Harden, B.J. Mullens and Robert Vaden in 2009 NBA Draft|date=June 26, 2009|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> He then played for the Thunder in both 2009 [[Orlando Summer League]] and [[NBA Summer League]]. He played in all five games in Orlando, averaging 3.0 points in 19.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/media/magic/okc_stats_071009.pdf|title=2009 Orlando Pro Summer League Stats: Oklahoma City Thunder Cumulative Stats|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> He improved his performance in the NBA Summer League, playing in all five games and averaging 7.8 points in 23.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2009/team/index.jsp?team=thunder|title=2009 NBA Summer League Team Page – Oklahoma City Thunder|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref> However, the Thunder didn't sign him to a contract and Vaden weighed the option to play overseas.<ref name="Silva">{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/vadenoverseas_100621.html|title=Vaden Eager to Display Improvements in His Game|first=Chris|last=Silva|date=June 21, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref>

Before the training camp began, Vaden signed a contract with [[Legadue Basket|Italian second division]] team [[Andrea Costa Imola|Aget Imola]]. On October 11, he scored 15 points in his first game for Imola, a 73–72 win over [[Dinamo Basket Sassari|Sassari]].<ref name="Silva"/> He played in 29 games and averaged 16.9 points on 40 percent shooting in 35.7 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/top_prospects_101031.html|title=2010 NBA D-League Draft – Top Prospects|first=Matthew|last=Brennan|date=October 31, 2010|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110101155331/http://www.nba.com/dleague/top_prospects_101031.html|archive-date=January 1, 2011}}</ref>

After one season in Italy, Vaden returned to the U.S. to participate in the [[2010 NBA Summer League|2010 Orlando Summer League]] with the Thunder. He played in all five games, averaging 4.6 points in 21.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2010/players/robert_vaden/index.html|title=2010 NBA Summer League Statistics – Robert Vaden|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 11, 2011}}</ref> However, he didn't receive a contract offer or an invitation to the Thunder's training camp for the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/roster_release100927.html|title=Thunder Announces Training Camp Roster|date=September 27, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 11, 2011}}</ref>

He then signed a contract to play in the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League) and became eligible for the [[2010 NBA Development League Draft|2010 D-League Draft]]. On November 1, 2010, Vaden was selected seventh overall by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/draft110110.html|title=Vipers Finalize Training Camp Roster with Eight Draftees|date=November 1, 2010|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117191205/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/draft110110.html|archive-date=November 17, 2010}}</ref> On the next day, he was traded to the [[Tulsa 66ers]], the D-League affiliate of the Thunder, in exchange for [[Mustafa Shakur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_acquire_vaden_2011_pick_2010_11_02.html|title=66ers Acquire Vaden, 2011 Pick|date=November 2, 2010|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 10, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111122113939/http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_acquire_vaden_2011_pick_2010_11_02.html|archive-date=November 22, 2011}}</ref> He played 45 games for the 66ers during the season, averaging 10.4 points on 39.2 percent shooting in 28.0 minutes per game. On April 9, 2011, after helping the 66ers win the first round of the D-League Playoffs against the [[Texas Legends]], he was signed by the Thunder and was immediately assigned back to the 66ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_vaden_110409.html|title=Thunder Signs Robert Vaden|date=April 9, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 11, 2011}}</ref> After the 66ers was eliminated from the second round of the playoffs, he was recalled by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_vaden_110420.html|title=Thunder Recalls Robert Vaden from Tulsa 66ers|date=April 20, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 21, 2011}}</ref>

During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Vaden played for [[BK SPU Nitra]] of Slovak basketball league on a three-month contract with an option to return to the NBA after the lockout ends.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/other-leagues/31142/robert_vaden_inks_in_slovakia_with_nitra_a_threemonth_contract.html|title=Robert Vaden inks in Slovakia with Nitra a three-month contract|date=September 21, 2011|work=Sportando.net|access-date=December 13, 2011}}</ref>

On December 13, 2011, the Thunder traded Vaden along with two future draft picks to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Lazar Hayward]]. After the trade, Vaden was immediately waived by the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/hayward_trade_okc_2011_12_13.html|title=Timberwolves Trade Lazar Hayward to Oklahoma City|date=December 13, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=December 13, 2011}}</ref>

On August 3, 2012, Vaden signed with [[Telekom Baskets Bonn]] of Germany's [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/41973/telekom-baskets-bonn-add-robert-vaden.html|title=Telekom Baskets Bonn add Robert Vaden|date=August 3, 2012|work=Sportando.net|access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref>

In 2013, Vaden signed with [[Belfius Mons-Hainaut]] of Belgium for the 2013–14 season.

On October 24, 2014, Vaden signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-robert-vaden|title=Spurs Sign Robert Vaden|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Spurs the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/2014/10/spurs-waive-jamychal-green-fuquan-edwin-robert-vaden/|title=Spurs waive JaMychal Green, Fuquan Edwin, Robert Vaden – NBA Blog – NBA Basketball Blog|date=October 25, 2014}}</ref> On November 1, 2014, he was selected by the [[Bakersfield Jam]] with the eighth overall pick in the 2014 NBA D-League draft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_jam_select_six_pla_2014_11_01.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128214736/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_jam_select_six_pla_2014_11_01.html|url-status=dead|title=Bakersfield Jam Select Six Players in 2014 NBA D-League Draft|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=January 28, 2015}}</ref> On January 20, 2015, he was traded to the [[Westchester Knicks]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Josh Owens]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-acquire-robert-vaden/n-4917843|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire Robert Vaden|date=January 20, 2015|website=OurSports Central}}</ref> On February 13, 2015, he was waived by Westchester due to a season-ending injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-acquire-two/n-4926879|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire Two|date=February 13, 2015|website=OurSports Central}}</ref>

On October 31, 2016, Vaden was re-acquired by the Westchester Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-finalize-2016-17-training-camp-roster/|title=Westchester Knicks Finalize 2016–17 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016}}</ref> On December 22, he was waived by Westchester after 11 games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Katie|last=Hatch|url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-activate-courtney-fells-waive-robert-vaden/|title=Westchester Knicks Activate Courtney Fells, Waive Robert Vaden|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 22, 2016|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> On January 23, 2017, Vaden was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |access-date=January 31, 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202074502/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=December 2, 2016 }}</ref> On March 28, 2017, he was waived by the BayHawks due to a season-ending concussion.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-acquire-joe-thomasson-waive-robert-vaden/|title=BayHawks Acquire Joe Thomasson, Waive Robert Vaden|work=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017}}</ref>
